newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE Brent may pare gains but well-supported.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE Brent may pare gains but well-supported.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+ IPE June Brent may pare Monday's 79 cent gain temporarily, but medium term uptrend intact.
+ June Brent well supported by break above trendline of Jan 9, 13 and Mar 19 highs and closure of $18.62/77 gap.
+ June gas oil expected to move sideways, price action around $174.25 seen as key.
IPE Brent futures were expected to move sideways to lower in the short-term, but many chartists said that in the medium term their recently re-found strength was intact.
June IPE Brent closed 10 cents lower at $19.62 a barrel on Tuesday, and was bid and offered at $19.25/$19.45 on SIMEX.
Technical analysts said that while bearish fundamentals could whittle away further at Monday's 79 cents gain on, technically the picture remained fairly firm in the medium-term.
June Brent was seen well supported by Monday's break above the trendline off the highs of January 9, 13 and March 19.
"It broke above there pretty strongly," said Darren Gurner at Sucden in London.
"I would expect to see some type of bullish flag formation taking shape over the next few days with increasingly small inside days ending with a breakout to the upside," said Gurner.
He said the contract's closure last week of the $18.62/77 gap which capped prices for about a month would also continue to lend support.
Gurner pegged support for the June Brent around $19.44 in line with Tuesday's low which is also close to the 38.2 percent retracemement level of the recent move higher at $19.46.
Below there, he saw support at $19.25 in line with where the trendline cuts the daily chart.
He noted upside targets around $20 and then $20.62.
Chartists at Elliott Wave International in Gainsville, Georgia were expecting further consolidation.
"Expect today's (Tuesday's) low to give way to a new high above $18.89. Then expect another period of sideways consolidation," they said in their global energy outlook.
They pegged support for June Brent at $19.65/61, $19.48, $19.40 and $18.67/43, and resistance at $19.70, $19.89, $19.91 and $20.65.
On the gas oil front, chartists were looking to a test of $174.25.

"Under a bullish or a bearish interpretation, the next event should be a test of the $174.25 peak. Then, look for a decline. The nature of this drop should help determine if the larger picture is bullish for a test of the $175.25/$177.25 peaks," Elliott Wave International said.
They pegged support for the contract at $172.25, $170.85 $165.25 and $164, and resistance at $174.25, $175.25, $176.50 and $177.25.
